teams.heading: Fiji lost 34-21 away to France in November 2025 friendly
teams.body: Fiji and France last met in a November 2025 International Friendly, with the Pacific side making the trip and losing. Fiji are 12th of 12 in the Nations Championship log after three matches, all defeats, scoring 49 and conceding 145 across them. They meet France again, as the hosts, at the Groupama Stadium in Lyon today.

teams.heading: Borthwick names Ben Curry and George Furbank in England side for Wallabies
teams.body: Ben Curry starts at openside against Australia, his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months, with Guy Pepper ruled out by an ankle injury sustained in Bath's defeat at Gloucester. George Furbank returns at full-back, Marcus Smith drops to the bench, and Fin Baxter starts at loosehead ahead of Ellis Genge. Maro Itoje is restored to the captaincy, and Exeter's Greg Fisilau is poised to win his first cap from the bench. Tom Curry misses the matchday 23 after an injury setback in training.

lead.why: The England team for Sunday's opener against Australia has just been named, with Ben Curry's return and George Furbank's recall as the headline changes.

teams.heading: Galthié reunites Dupont and Ntamack as France's half-back pairing against Fiji
teams.body: Coach Fabien Galthié has named Antoine Dupont at scrum-half and Romain Ntamack at flyhalf for Saturday's match in Lyon, their first start together at half-back since March 2025. Ntamack's injury record includes a long-running kidney problem, while Dupont missed the whole of July with a calf issue. Matthieu Jalibert is out with a quadriceps problem, and Maxime Lucu is among the replacements. Fiji, coached by Jake White, scored no points in July, losing 39-24 to Wales and 73-8 to England.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell faces injury worries after Dan Sheehan fails head assessment
teams.body: Captain Dan Sheehan was forced off in the first half of Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina after failing a head injury assessment, though Andy Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room". Robert Baloucoune also left with a knock in the 58th minute, while Sean Jansen took a "bang" to his knee and Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns. Hansen continued after treatment.

teams.heading: Nacho Brex calls Springboks' De Allende and Kriel probably the best pairing
teams.body: Italy's vice-captain Juan Ignacio Brex, sidelined for Saturday's match, has praised Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel. "They're probably the best centre partnership in the world," he told Planet Rugby exclusively. Brex, who detached a bicep in the last Top 14 round and expects surgery next week, said he and Tommaso Menoncello see the South African pair as a benchmark to challenge. Menoncello, who faces 12 weeks out after subluxing his shoulder for Toulouse against Exeter Chiefs in the Champions Cup, is also out.

teams.heading: Josh Kerr to deliver match ball before Scotland face All Blacks
teams.body: Olympic silver medallist Josh Kerr will deliver the match ball to the middle of the Murrayfield pitch before Saturday's Test, and he has already been inside the camp. He joined the squad for Friday's captain's run and a lunch session on high performance, and told the Telegraph he would "look awful" on the pitch, joking that his speed would let him down. His brother Jake won a full cap at hooker for Scotland in 2019.

teams.heading: Bill Sweeney confirms WRU's formal request for Welsh clubs to join Prem
teams.body: The Welsh Rugby Union wants its clubs in English rugby's top flight, and the RFU has confirmed the request. Speaking to BBC Radio Four, chief executive Bill Sweeney said the RFU had "received a formal approach" and must go back with more questions. Its stated focus remains expanding the English game, with the Premiership moving from 10 to 12 clubs. The United Rugby Championship has threatened the WRU, a shareholder, with legal action over leaving.

lead.why: A fresh, confirmed WRU move with a direct stake for Wales, unlike the Griffin training story already published.

teams.heading: Bath sign Argentina tight-head prop Marcos Camerlinckx, Super Rugby Americas champion
teams.body: Marcos Camerlinckx, a 22-year-old tight-head prop and former Argentina Under-20 international, joins Bath after winning this year's Super Rugby Americas Championship with Pampas XV. He also played for an Argentina XV against the United States in August. Bath director of rugby Johann van Graan told the club website: "We are looking forward to seeing how Marcos will develop his game over the next period of time and I am sure he will fit into our group very well." Bath have not disclosed the length of the deal.

lead.why: It is the only new item about an Argentina player, and the Ireland match report has already run today.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight to win 50th cap as Wallabies name Len Ikitau back
teams.body: Jeremy Williams starts at blindside in a new-look back row for Sunday's Test against England at Twickenham, with Fraser McReight winning his 50th cap alongside Williams and Harry Wilson captaining from number eight. Len Ikitau returns to midfield after missing the last Test under HIA protocols, partnering Isaac Henry, who will play his first Test in the United Kingdom. Taniela Tupou is back among the replacements.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones starts uncapped Riku Kitahara at fly-half against Wales
teams.body: Japan have been without their first three choice fly-halves for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Wales. Eddie Jones has opted to start Riku Kitahara, uncapped and from Honda Heat, at fly-half. Shinya Komura, who won his last of three caps against Georgia in November 2025, is the only other fly-half on tour. Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee are injured, while Ryunosuke Ito, who has started every Japan Test in 2026, is back at university and misses the entire tour.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett's form could cause selection headaches, Jeff Wilson says
teams.body: Former All Blacks full-back Jeff Wilson has pointed to Beauden Barrett's recent form. Injuries to Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga opened the door, with Barrett coming in at 15 and Damian McKenzie moving from full-back to take Love and Mo'unga's place, and the pair have kept their spots. Wilson said: "If he continues his good form, I think it will be him who might give the selectors headaches because their preferred option was clearly McKenzie at 15."

lead.why: A fresh New Zealand selection story about the 10 and 15 positions, which the earlier Wilson pieces did not cover.

teams.heading: Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to test uncapped Boks against France, Ireland
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus named South Africa's strongest available side for the Italy match, holding back six uncapped players, including Yaqeen Ahmed, Markus Muller, Riley Norton and Luan Giliomee. His explanation was time: the group only arrived in camp on Monday. Victor Matfield, speaking on the Rivals podcast, expects those players to be involved later in the tougher Nations Championship tests, adding that the head coach is never shy of a selection curveball.

lead.why: A fresh selection story about South Africa's own uncapped players, which fits the brief better than the Brex quote already reported today.
